_comment: Pinned on purpose: a system driver (xess-xmx-linux) and ClawDeck's own OptiScaler + OptiPatcher are installed only at a tested version (OptiScaler with its sha256); 'pending-verification' asks before installing the latest. tools/upstream_watch.py reports newer ones.

xess_xmx_linux.note: 20261107: hardening of the driver, shim and hook, the other missing kernels compiled in the background on a cache miss, Mesa 26.3 patch 0006 (a Cyberpunk 2077 crash), the session check run from ~/.config/xess-xmx (stock drivers when the package folder is gone), any case of the prefix driver store; the session file, hook mark and shim path ClawDeck reads are unchanged. Also an experimental Vulkan layer for the stock driver (xmx-stock.sh), not used by ClawDeck yet. 20261104: low latency with XeSS frame generation on by default (IGDEXT_XELL_CAP), FSR 3.1+ games on XeSS (FSR=xess), XESS_FG up to 8x

decky_framegen.note: v0.17 (OptiScaler 0.9.4, FSR 4 variants) installed and opened on the Claw 8 EX 2026-11-04. OptiScaler per game (Bazzite ships it in the Portal); ClawDeck installs it only where it is missing, and passes Intel presets to it through its environment variables

reframework.note: Capcom RE Engine games: dinput8.dll (23252480 bytes, REFramework 0.1.0.69) next to the game's exe. onehoon's fork (the fork's author), release 15 built 2026-10-22, whose notes say to use it with OptiScaler in Capcom games: a working Windows Onimusha install runs exactly this file, and it booted and played with optiscaler_v10 on a Claw 8 EX on Bazzite (2026-11-04). Replaces praydog's nightly 01433: ClawDeck installs REFramework only together with the Capcom OptiScaler setup, and the fork is the build that setup was tested with. Release 18 (2026-11-05) since 2026-11-09: three upstream syncs over release 15 (Lua JSON and LooseFileLoader fixes, HookManager error paths and thread safety, ARM64EC hooks skipped), dinput8.dll 23262720 bytes; release 15's dll stays recognised (previous_dll_sha256) so Remove still takes it out.

optiscaler.note: ClawDeck's own OptiScaler (optiscaler.py): the same release and OptiPatcher build Decky Framegen v0.17 pins, with the same sha256.

optiscaler_v10.note: Capcom RE Engine games only (optiscaler.py layout 'subfolder'): OptiScaler.dll as the proxy and OptiScaler.ini next to the exe, everything else in OptiScaler\ (OptiDllPath), OptiPatcher in OptiScaler\plugins. a working Windows Onimusha install uses 0.9.5-pre4, which isn't published on GitHub; this public v10 nightly ran Onimusha with onehoon's REFramework on a Claw 8 EX on Bazzite (2026-11-04). Every other game stays on 'optiscaler' (0.9.4). fakenvapi v1.4.1 (FakeMichau) goes in OptiScaler\ with the tested fakenvapi.ini, as in the tested folder: its fakenvapi.dll (415232 bytes) is byte-identical to the one OptiScaler 0.9.4 ships. OptiScaler v10 has fakenvapi built in ([fakenvapi] UseFakenvapi, set to true) and doesn't load the file; it is there to match the setup tested on the Claw.

fsr4_xmx.note: nitec's FSR 4.1.2 build for the XMX cores (OptiScaler community), shared with ClawDeck with nitec's OK (maintainer, 2026-11-05), the same files the tested setup installs on Intel (its Archives/Custom/FSR4_XMX). Hosted on ClawDeck's fsr4-xmx-files branch, pinned by commit (not on the Releases page); downloaded into ~/fsr4-xmx when missing, each sha256 checked (the maintainer's working copy on the Claw 8 EX, 2026-11-04).
